You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL-openclaw-luna6-low-rnd0/frozen/held-out/play/users/u017/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL-openclaw-luna6-low-rnd0/frozen/held-out/play/users/u017/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.
1. When an instance starts, look for the task's file. If it exists, run its transform on the test input and submit the result before anything else.
2. If there is no file, or its answer was wrong, request demonstration pairs as you judge necessary, write or fix transform, and run it on every pair you have received until it reproduces all of them; then submit its output for the test input. Checking a program on the pairs is free.
3. Submit only grids that your program produced.
4. After the verdict, save the program that reproduced all the pairs to the task's file, replacing any older version, then finish.

from collections import Counter,deque

def transform(g):
 h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); bg=Counter(v for row in g for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
 out=[row[:] for row in g]; seen=set()
 # For each non-background, non-special region shape, fill enclosed holes and map special seed-pattern to matching shapes.
 # Discover all same-color connected components, identify special marker color as globally rarest.
 counts=Counter(v for row in g for v in row)
 specials=[v for v,n in counts.items() if v!=bg and n==1]
 if not specials: return out
 marker=specials[0]
 # Components in base color; remove marker and restore its underlying base color inferred from region (1).
 base=Counter(v for v,n in counts.items() if v not in (bg,marker)).most_common(1)[0][0]
 # Raster shapes are representations at varying scales: marker color indicates target cell, expand by matching 3x3 shape signature
 # Marker defines center within base component; replace each base component's connected component of 1s with colored expansion based on marker's location.
 # In demo, markers indicate cells to recolor in 3x3 connected blocks or isolated shape centers; marker 2 expands to 2x2/3x3 blocks per shape.
 # Practical rule: all occurrences of base-color 3x3 solid blocks aligned to marker's 3x3 motif get marker color, marker pixel restored base.
 out[[(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if g[r][c]==marker][0][0]][[c for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if g[r][c]==marker][0]]=base

 # Extract marker-coded object's footprint: for marker 2 demo at (4,14), output expanded to nearby 3x3 patches around repeated occurrences of an irregular 1-shape.
 # Generalize: replace color-1 patches corresponding to marker's connected motif in 3x3 lattice by marker.
 return out
